explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge (LITRANSPROQA) with human evaluation results, reporting correlation metrics (ACC-EQ and Kendall's τ) between LLM judgments and human assessments across multiple datasets

prompts.notes: Vanilla template: 'You are a professional literary translator with extensive experience. Now you are translating a work of great aesthetic value and cultural significance. You need to check if the translation covers all translation aspects by answering YES, NO or MAYBE to the following questions. Please be honest with your assessment and consider all aspects of translation quality.' PromptStep template includes step-by-step instructions. Questions cover 6 literary aspects.

inter_annotator_agreement.interpretation: Distribution shown but no single aggregated value provided

guidelines.notes: Used Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) framework with professional translators rating questions on scale of 5. Appendix includes survey instructions and question evaluation criteria.

sample_size.notes: Evaluation conducted on three datasets: LITEVAL-CORPUS (over 2k paragraphs), LITERARYTRAN (540 pairwise annotations), PAR3-ANNOTATED (372 comparison cases)

validation_results.summary_finding: LITRANSPROQA substantially outperforms SOTA metrics with up to 0.07 gain in correlation and 15-23 point gains in adequacy, approaching trained student evaluator performance but still lagging behind experienced professional translators.

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluation uses 25 selected questions covering 6 literary aspects, while human evaluation uses MQM framework and professional translator insights. Both evaluate overall translation quality on the same datasets.
